title: Config activation safeguard orchestration for batching & cache recommendations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective:
Create an orchestrator that safely applies batching and caching recommendations generated by Optimize while providing deterministic rollback and clear operator controls. The orchestrator must minimize manual toil, limit customer risk, and surface measurable savings and regressions before and after activation.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: suggestion adoption pipeline (policy evaluation, dry-run simulation, staged activation, telemetry gating, approval handshake, automatic rollback), Console UI for approvals and audit trail, and runtime hooks for emergency aborts.
- Non-goal: fully autonomous tuning without human-in-the-loop for enterprise customers; we will provide conservative defaults and an opt-in fully-automatic mode later.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Preflight simulation: run suggestions in a dry-run mode against historical traffic slices (prefixes/seq-len cohorts) to estimate token savings, latency delta, and error rates. Produce a preflight report and an expected cost-savings curve.
2) Policy engine: express rules as simple predicates (max-latency-delta, error-rate-rise, min-savings) and a staged rollout plan (percentages timeline + escalation). Customers or org defaults can pick policy profiles: Strict, Balanced, Aggressive.
3) Staged activation choreography: (a) Canary (2%) with mirrored traffic + passive validation, (b) Ramp to 10% with active tracing, (c) Full rollout if telemetry passes. Each stage has time windows and automatic gating.
4) Telemetry gating: integrate with Console metrics and runtime tracing. Gate evaluation uses rolling windows (5m/30m) and statistical thresholds (p95 latency change, regression in reranking accuracy proxies). Telemetry failures trigger automatic rollback to previous config and create an incident in Ops.
5) Operator acknowledgement: for Strict/enterprise profiles, require operator approval after the preflight before canary; for Balanced allow auto-canary but require manual approval to reach full rollout. Approvals recorded with metadata (actor, timestamp, rationale).
6) Safe rollback and escape hatches: immediate kill-switch (global or per-customer), automatic revert if thresholds breached, and staged-based rollback (rollback to last known-good configuration).
7) Observability and audit: store preflight reports, rollout history, metrics snapshots, and associated GitHub PRs in Console. Expose an endpoint for customers to fetch the rollout timeline and decision logs.

Trade-offs noted during scoping:
- Complexity vs. safety: richer policies increase surface area and testing burden; we start with a predicate-based engine instead of a full policy DSL.
- Simulation fidelity: dry-run against historical traffic is cheaper than full canary simulation but may miss emerging workload patterns; mitigate with mirrored-canary stage.
- Ops burden: more stages reduce risk but lengthen deployment; default profiles balance safety and speed.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1-2: Preflight simulation service + preflight report schema (backend) 
- Week 3: Policy engine prototype + sample policy profiles
- Week 4: Canary runner (mirrored traffic path) + telemetry hooks (p95/p99, error-rate, token-usage)
- Week 5: Approval workflow API + Console approval UI mockups
- Week 6: Rollout orchestration + rollback paths + tests
- Week 7: End-to-end QA, security review, and canary on internal workloads

Open design questions / risks:
- Which metric proxies best capture "quality" regressions for opaque models? (currently evaluating BLEU-like proxies, per-customer eval sets, and token-entropy heuristics)
- Allowed rollback latency: how quickly must we return to previous config for large fleets? Target is sub-30s automated rollback but needs infra validation.
- Access controls: enterprise customers require SAML/SCIM-based RBAC gating for approval actions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Preflight reports generated for 95% of suggestions within 10m of request
- Canary runner can mirror 2% of production requests to a sandboxed path without affecting user-visible latency
- Gate evaluation will trigger rollback if p95 latency increases by >20ms or error-proxy increases by >1.5x over baseline
- Console shows rollout audit trail and approval history for each adoption event

Deliverables and artifacts:
- Confluence: design doc (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Config+Activation+Orchestrator)
- GH PRs: backend prototype (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7821), console UI (https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/614)
